title: ALLMod: Exploring Area-Efficiency of LUT-based Large Number Modular Reduction via Hybrid Workloads
problem: Cryptographic applications (homomorphic encryption, zero-knowledge proofs) require high-bit-width modular reduction (128–8192 bits), which is compute-intensive. LUT-based approaches reduce computation via lookup tables but incur significant hardware area overhead due to extensive LUT storage.
method: ALLMod improves area efficiency of LUT-based modular reduction by employing hybrid workloads: decomposes the bit-group segmentation into two distinct workloads (inspired by iterative reduction), balances their distribution via a template, and uses design space exploration to find optimal timing for fusing results. Trades computation across workloads to reduce LUT storage while maintaining throughput.

title: TB-STC: Transposable Block-wise N:M Structured Sparse Tensor Core
problem: Existing N:M structured sparsity for DNN accelerators causes significant accuracy degradation (e.g., >6% on OPT-6.7B and Llama2-7B at 50% sparsity) because one-dimensional structured sparsity patterns diverge far from the unstructured optimal. Hardware support for sparsity must simultaneously deliver high bandwidth utilization and computational efficiency.
method: The paper introduces Transposable Block-wise Structured (TBS) sparsity, which exploits the transpose relationship between forward and backward pass weight matrices during training to find a 2D block sparsity pattern that more closely approximates unstructured sparsity. At the micro-architecture level, TB-STC implements a Transposable Block-wise N:M Sparse Tensor Core with an adaptive codec for on-the-fly storage format conversion supporting both row-wise and column-wise sparse access, and an I/O-aware configurable scheduler for sparsity-aware compute scheduling. This enables 1.47x bandwidth utilization and 1.57x computational utilization improvements.

title: A 38.1Mb/mm2 SRAM in a 2nm-CMOS-Nanosheet Technology for High-Density and Energy-Efficient Compute
problem: Scaling SRAM bit-cell area at advanced nodes faces diminishing returns; peripheral circuits dominate area overhead, and maintaining reliability at reduced cell voltage becomes challenging.
method: Design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) leveraging 2nm nanosheet technology's improved on/off-current ratio to increase BL loading capacity by 2x, allowing denser memory bit arrays per peripheral circuit. Special logic rules and floor-planning techniques optimize both cell and peripheral area while maintaining reliability margins.

title: McPAL: Scaling Unstructured Sparse Inference with Multi-Chiplet HBM-PIM Architecture for LLMs
problem: Monolithic PIM architectures cannot scale to very large LLMs (70B+) due to single-die memory footprint limits; LLM inference is memory-bound, and PIM can provide high memory bandwidth but scaling via larger dies hits power/yield constraints.
method: Multi-chiplet HBM-PIM architecture (McPAL) that decomposes arbitrary unstructured sparse weight matrices into multiple irregular sparse vectors, then routes non-skipped computations via in-memory butterfly network to standard PIM arrays. Vertically scales via 3D-HBM hierarchy (minimizing long-distance data travel) and horizontally via 2.5D IO chiplet (reducing die-to-die traffic and balancing sparse workload).

title: D-VSync: Decoupled Rendering and Displaying for Smartphone Graphics
problem: The VSync-based rendering architecture on smartphones tightly couples the rendering pipeline to the display refresh cycle, causing frame drops and increased rendering latency when large high-frame-rate screens and complex visual effects (physics-based animations, stunning UI) demand rendering time that exceeds the VSync interval. This rigid coupling prevents flexible scheduling of rendering work across display periods.
method: D-VSync decouples the rendering pipeline from the display refresh cycle by separating the rendering scheduler from the VSync signal, allowing rendering to be completed asynchronously relative to display timing. The system introduces a buffering and synchronization layer that permits rendering jobs to run beyond a single VSync period and uses predictive scheduling to align rendered frames with the nearest available display window, reducing the frequency of missed frames.

title: ZXNet: ZX Calculus-Driven Graph Neural Network Framework for Quantum Circuit Equivalence Checking
problem: Quantum circuits require transpilation into hardware-compatible instructions, significantly altering designs; existing equivalence checking methods struggle with scalability and computational overhead.
method: ZXNet integrates ZX calculus with graph neural networks for quantum circuit equivalence checking. ZX calculus provides compact graph abstractions of quantum circuits, while GNNs capture complex equivalence patterns by learning both local and global circuit features. The framework leverages ZX-based graph representations to reduce dimensionality and complexity of the equivalence checking problem.

title: NUPEA: Optimizing Critical Loads on Spatial Dataflow Architectures via Non-Uniform Processing-Element Access
problem: On large spatial dataflow architectures (SDAs) where program instructions are distributed across a fabric of processing elements (PEs), some PEs are physically closer to memory than others, creating non-uniform data access latencies (NUPEA). Existing approaches focused on NUMA-style data placement, which is complex and often ineffective when critical data is hard to identify statically.
method: NUPEA observes that on large SDAs, placing critical load instructions on PEs physically close to memory reduces data movement costs. The authors implement architecture extensions and compiler optimizations for NUPEA on the Monaco SDA (by Efficient Computer) and its effcc compiler. The compiler identifies critical loads via dependence analysis and maps them to near-memory PEs, while the architecture exposes PE-to-memory proximity information to the compiler. This contrasts with NUMA where data is moved closer to fixed PEs.

title: Energy-aware Scheduling and Input Buffer Overflow Prevention for Energy-harvesting Systems
problem: Energy-harvesting IoT devices capture data at a fixed rate but process it at a dynamically varying rate determined by available ambient power; when capture rate exceeds processing rate the fixed-size input buffer overflows and events are permanently lost, and no existing dynamic solution prevents this across varying energy and workload conditions.
method: Quetzal combines a hardware power-measurement circuit with a two-part software runtime. The energy-aware scheduler selects jobs by minimizing end-to-end latency including projected energy recharging time, not just execution time. The runtime uses queueing-theory models to predict whether the selected job will cause an input buffer overflow before it completes; if overflow is imminent, it degrades the scheduled job (e.g., reduces quality or shortens duration) to lower processing latency and prevent buffer saturation. The hardware circuit is simple and system-agnostic, providing real-time power readings to the scheduler.

title: DyREM: Dynamically Mitigating Quantum Readout Error with Embedded Accelerator
problem: Quantum readout error mitigation requires on-the-fly computation of large mitigation matrices, incurring high latency and memory overhead that limits practical quantum computing scale.
method: DyREM leverages sparsity in quantum state probability distributions to dynamically downsample mitigation matrices. An embedded accelerator computes tensor products using gating to skip nonzero quantum state computations.

title: Accelerating design-technology co-development using neural compact modeling and data-driven SPICE simulation
problem: Design-technology co-optimization requires rapid iteration between circuit designers and technology developers, but slow PDK (process design kit) release cycles and long SPICE simulation times create bottlenecks. Compact models are needed for fast, accurate feedback in technology development.
method: The framework uses neural compact modeling (NCM) combined with data-driven SPICE simulation. Pre-trained NCM models are efficiently retargeted for new process variants using fine-tuning. Data interpolation and derating techniques recreate design environments (instance binning, process variations, layout-dependent effects) without running SPICE. Fast feedback enables rapid exploration during technology optimization.

title: 26.4 A 24-to-29GHz Compact Transmit/Receive Front-End Module Featuring an Asymmetric Doherty Power Amplifier and 0.22mm2 Area
problem: Mm-wave FEMs must simultaneously achieve high TX linearity/efficiency and low RX noise figure while remaining compact. Conventional Class-AB PAs provide <10% TX PAE under OFDM signals with 10dB PAPR, limiting overall system efficiency.
method: An asymmetric Doherty power amplifier (DPA) design provides high efficiency under modulated signals through dynamic bias adjustment and impedance modulation. The FEM integrates PA, LNA, and T/R switch in a 0.22mm² footprint for 24-29GHz operation.

title: Understanding RowHammer Under Reduced Refresh Latency: Experimental Analysis of Real DRAM Chips and Implications on Future Solutions
problem: RowHammer mitigations based on preventive refresh incur growing performance and energy overheads as DRAM technology scaling reduces the activation threshold for bit-flip induction. The interaction between refresh latency and RowHammer vulnerability in real DRAM chips has not been rigorously characterized.
method: The authors perform the first experimental characterization of refresh-latency vs. RowHammer interactions on 388 real DDR4 chips from three manufacturers, varying preventive refresh (tRFM) latency below nominal values. They find that refresh latency can be reduced by 64% with only a 0.54% increase in required refresh count. Building on these findings, they design PaCRAM (Partial Charge Restoration for Aggressive Mitigation), a mechanism that reduces tRFM for preventive refreshes and compensates by slightly increasing refresh frequency, thus lowering the performance tax of five state-of-the-art RowHammer defenses.

title: Insights from Rights and Wrongs: A Large Language Model for Solving Assertion Failures in RTL Design
problem: Assertion failures in SystemVerilog RTL designs require manual analysis of complex logical and timing relationships between signals to identify and fix the underlying issues. No automated tool currently assists engineers in solving these failures.
method: AssertSolver is a specialized LLM trained on synthetic data from challenging test cases and incorporating error feedback. It analyzes assertion failures and RTL code to predict bug fixes and design corrections, achieving an 88.54% bug-fixing pass@1 metric on the test suite.

title: Few-shot Learning on AMS Circuits and Its Application to Parasitic Capacitance Prediction
problem: Predicting parasitic capacitance in analog/mixed-signal (AMS) circuit designs is critical for performance and power, but deep learning models require large labeled datasets that are scarce in IC design. Few-shot learning can exploit limited labeled data, but scalability and practical applicability remain open challenges.
method: CircuitGPS uses graph representation learning with heterogeneous graphs (nodes: circuit components, links: coupling capacitance) and a hybrid Transformer for subgraph embedding learning. Pre-trains on link prediction (does capacitance coupling exist?), fine-tunes on edge regression (coupling magnitude). Uses small-hop sampling to create subgraphs and low-cost positional encoding capturing structural information.

title: Frugal: Efficient and Economic Embedding Model Training with Commodity GPUs
problem: Embedding model training on commodity GPUs (those lacking high-bandwidth inter-GPU interconnects and PCIe peer-to-peer support) suffers poor performance due to communication bottlenecks: sparse embedding lookups generate irregular, small-sized all-to-all communication that overwhelms limited commodity GPU network bandwidth. This makes cost-effective training on low-end GPU clusters impractical despite their cheap compute for the memory-intensive embedding workload.
method: Frugal addresses communication bottlenecks through a combination of: (1) communication-aware embedding table partitioning that minimizes cross-GPU sparse lookup traffic, (2) compression or aggregation of embedding gradients to reduce bandwidth demand over commodity interconnects, and (3) scheduling that overlaps compute and communication phases to hide latency. The system is designed for the constraint of no PCIe P2P, routing communication through CPU host memory when necessary.

title: DeepContext: A Context-aware, Cross-platform, and Cross-framework Tool for Performance Profiling and Analysis of Deep Learning Workloads
problem: Existing DL profiling tools fail to bridge the semantic gap between high-level Python/framework operations and low-level GPU execution, making it difficult to identify the root cause of performance bottlenecks across the full software stack. No existing tool provides correlated, context-aware profiling spanning Python, DL frameworks, C/C++ libraries, and GPU kernels simultaneously.
method: DeepContext uses a framework-agnostic shim layer that intercepts calls between the DL framework and underlying C/C++ libraries, correlating them with GPU hardware performance metrics and Python-level program context. This shim layer enables causal linking of high-level operator invocations to their low-level GPU execution without modifying framework source code. An automated performance analyzer then processes the correlated trace to generate actionable optimization guidance.
